{{Top}}
[[File:KharrusBurial-GG.png|thumb|right|300px|The burial site of Senator Kharrus on Florrum]]
'''Burial''' was one of the procedures used throughout most of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] to dispose of the [[Death/Legends|remains]] of [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] creatures. Sentients were buried underground and the location marked with a [[tombstone]], or entombed inside of crypts. A variation of this was [[Realspace/Legends|space]] burial&mdash;in which the deceased was sealed inside a casket and this casket was then launched into space. An alternative to burial was [[Cremation/Legends|cremation]], or the disposal of remains by burning them, which was another popular method of disposing of the remains of deceased sentients.

The [[Sacorria]]n moon of [[Sarcophagus]] was entirely devoted to being a burial ground for the [[Planet/Legends|planet]]. On [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] the [[Senatorial Tombs]] was the final resting place of many Senators, many of whom were [[Carbon-freezing/Legends|frozen]] in [[Carbonite/Legends|carbonite]] and interred in the tombs. [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Viento]] was buried in this manner after his [[Assassin/Legends|assassination]] in [[20 BBY/Legends|20 BBY]].

Space burial was a popular method of disposal, especially for military personnel. [[Lujayne Forge]] was one person who was buried in space. Following her death [[6 ABY/Legends|6.5 years]] after the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]] during an attack on the [[Rogue Squadron/Legends|Rogue Squadron]] base on [[Talasea]] by [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]], she and the other six sentries who had been killed in the attack were buried in space after a memorial service on board the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] [[Starship/Legends|ship]] ''[[Reprieve]]''.

According to [[Lobot/Legends|Lobot]], there were were twenty-two thousand, four hundred eight known cultures which entombed riches with the dead by the time of the [[Black Fleet Crisis]].

==Cultures==
A number of different cultures practiced burial in varying forms.

===Sith===
Many of the early [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] [[Sith Lord/Legends|Lords]] were given elaborate burials in the [[Valley of the Dark Lords/Legends|Valley of the Dark Lords]] on [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]]. Even though the tombs were equipped with traps and other defenses, the tombs were eventually penetrated and most of the artifacts were removed from the tombs. The Sith Lord [[Ludo Kressh]] was not buried in the Valley of the Dark Lords, he was buried in a [[Tomb of Ludo Kressh|secret tomb]] inside a large [[Shyrack cave]] on Korriban. That tomb was filled with dark side energy, which caused visitors to experience massive hallucinations, which were so vivid that visitors were unable to tell whether they were real or not.

While most of the ancient Sith Lords were buried on Korriban, this was not always the case. The Sith Lord [[Freedon Nadd]] was [[Tomb of Freedon Nadd|buried]] on [[Dxun/Legends|Dxun]], which orbited [[Onderon/Legends|Onderon]].

===Jedi===
[[File:Flowers_for_Shmi.jpg|thumb|left|Shmi Skywalker's grave on Tatooine]]
In most cases, [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] were generally not buried. Rather, deceased Jedi were often [[Cremation/Legends|cremated]] on a pyre. In rare cases the body of a Jedi faded away after death&mdash;as happened with both Masters [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]] and [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]].

After [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] reestablished the Jedi Order, a number of Jedi were buried in a grove in the Yavin jungle, with a gray plinth marking the graves. [[Gantoris]] was the first to be buried there, followed by [[Dorsk 81]], and in time they would be joined by many others.

The [[The Barsen'thor|third Barsen'thor]] of the Jedi Order was buried following his death in a [[Chandrila Jedi tomb|massive tomb]] on [[Chandrila/Legends|Chandrila]].<ref name="Force and Destiny Rulebook">[[Star Wars: Force and Destiny Core Rulebook|''Star Wars: Force and Destiny'' Core Rulebook]]</ref> [[14 ABY/Legends|Fourteen years]] after the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], [[Jaden Korr]] was sent on a [[Mission to Chandrila|mission]] to prevent the [[Disciples of Ragnos]] from siphoning the power from the tomb. The Disciples were able to unseal the Jedi Master's coffin, but were stopped from stealing the power by Korr. He proceeded to reseal the coffin, but the tomb collapsed shortly afterward.

===Mandalorian===
On [[Mandalore/Legends|Mandalore]], most [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorians]] were buried as simply as possible within mass graves that had no markers. Some highly placed individuals, such as [[Mandalore (title)/Legends|Mandalore]], were offered the option of having a marked grave. However, Boba Fett wished to just set the [[Slave I/Legends|''Slave I'']] on [[Autopilot/Legends|autopilot]] and just drift in space.

After removing his [[Jango Fett/Legends|father's]] remains from [[Geonosis/Legends|Geonosis]], [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]] buried them on Mandalore, along with those of his [[Ailyn Vel|daughter]].

===Necropolitan===

Burial was considered a sacred rite on the world of [[Necropolis (Core Worlds)|Necropolis]], and most Necropolitans buried their dead instead of opting for methods such as cremation. As a result, much of Necropolis was covered with gravesites, and the world became known for its large amount of burials. Necropolitans also believed that bad things would happen if the proper funeral and burial rites were not followed, and not burying a body was considered an act of sacrilege. The bodies were usually placed within coffins, which were subsequently buried in the ground, and the graves were usually adorned with headstones containing inscriptions.<ref name="Galaxy of Fear: City of the Dead">''[[Galaxy of Fear: City of the Dead]]''</ref>
